title: Ready for Year 7? A friendly Maths check
seo_title: Ready for Year 7? Free Maths check for Year 6 (ages 10 to 11)
description: A free, friendly 24-question Maths check for Year 6 children starting secondary school. No timer and no sign-up. Shows which areas are ready and which to practise first, with links to free practice.
intro: 24 questions about the Maths you'll use on day one of secondary school. There's no timer and no pass or fail. At the end you'll see what you're ready for and where to practise next.

questions.explain: From the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands. The 6 is in the hundred thousands column, so it is worth 600,000.
Look at the hundreds digit: 5. That means round up, so 74,562 rounds to 75,000.

questions.q: The temperature is −3 °C. It rises by 8 degrees. What is the new temperature, in °C?
questions.explain: From −3 it takes 3 degrees to reach 0, then 5 more: 5 °C.
4,508 + 2,797 = 7,305. (Check: 4,500 + 2,800 = 7,300, so the answer should be close to that.)
Multiply the top and bottom by 2: {3/4} = {6/8}.
The bottom numbers are the same, so add the tops: 2 + 1 = 3. The answer is {3/5}.
The 3 is in the tenths column, so 0.3 = {3/10}. (It's also 30%.)
50% means half. Half of 64 is 32.

questions.q: How many grams are in 2.5 kg?
A film starts at 18:40 and lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. When does it end?
questions.explain: 18:40 + 1 hour = 19:40. 20 more minutes takes you to 20:00, and 15 more to 20:15.

questions.q: You buy 3 notebooks at £1.45 each and pay with a £10 note. How much change do you get, in pounds?
Two angles in a triangle are 35° and 85°. What is the third angle?
questions.explain: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 180 − 35 − 85 = 60°.

questions.q: What is the area of a rectangle 9 cm long and 7 cm wide?
questions.explain: Area = length × width = 9 × 7 = 63 cm².

questions.q: Which shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
options: A rectangle that is not a square
questions.explain: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry. A square has 4, an equilateral triangle 3 and a kite 1.
The numbers go up by 4 each time. 15 + 4 = 19.
Work backwards: 23 − 3 = 20, and 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Check: 5 × 4 + 3 = 23.

questions.q: Cost in pounds = 3 × number of rides. How many pounds do 7 rides cost?
questions.explain: 3 × 7 = 21, so 7 rides cost £21.
